Every `omniglass` command, generated from the binary's own command tree. The data commands
are generated from the [API](/reference/api/) (`make gen`), so this reference is a faithful mirror of
what the server exposes. For the narrative, connecting, authenticating, and the generated-versus-
hand-written split, see [the CLI guide](/guides/cli/).

## Global flags

Every command accepts these. An omitted flag falls back to its environment variable, read when the command runs, so this page and every `--help` name the variable and never print its value:

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--server` | string | `http://localhost:8080` | Omniglass server base URL; when omitted, $OMNIGLASS_SERVER, else the default |
| `--token` | string | (none) | bearer token; when omitted, $OMNIGLASS_TOKEN (read at run time, never printed) |

## `omniglass action-rule`

Commands for the action-rule resource

### `omniglass action-rule create`

Create an action rule

```
omniglass action-rule create [flags]
```

Adds a rule that, on an alarm's raise or clear, when its predicate holds over the alarm facts, queues one notification per target in the transition's own transaction, which the server's tick then delivers. An unknown transition, type or target, or a predicate that does not compile, is a 422; a taken name a 409. Audited. Gated by rule:create, with an all-scope grant: a rule watches the whole fleet.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--description` | string | (none) | What it is for |
| `--enabled` | bool | `false` | Whether it fires (default true): a disabled rule queues nothing on a transition, and what it queued before still delivers |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A human label |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The rule's name (lowercase kebab) |
| `--notification-type` | string | (none) | The notification type to send, by name or uuid; absent sends the official one for the transition |
| `--on` | string | (none) | The alarm transitions it fires on: raised, cleared, or both. Acknowledging an alarm is never one |
| `--opt-out-allowed` | bool | `false` | Let a member of a group it targets opt out of it for themselves (default false) |
| `--targets` | string | (none) | The notification targets to send to, by name or uuid |
| `--when` | string | (none) | A predicate over the alarm facts at the action expression site (component, place, severity, severity_rank, message, transition, rule, ...; see /expressions:validate with site action); absent always holds. A refusal is a 422 with its line and column |

Example:

```sh
omniglass action-rule create --name name --on <json> --targets <json>
```

### `omniglass action-rule delete`

Delete an action rule

```
omniglass action-rule delete <name>
```

Removes a rule; the notifications it queued keep its name. Audited. Gated by rule:delete, with an all-scope grant.

Example:

```sh
omniglass action-rule delete <name>
```

### `omniglass action-rule get`

Get an action rule

```
omniglass action-rule get <name>
```

Returns one action rule by name or uuid. Gated by rule:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass action-rule get <name>
```

### `omniglass action-rule list`

List action rules

```
omniglass action-rule list
```

Lists every action rule, by name: on which alarm transitions, when, and what it sends to which targets. Gated by rule:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass action-rule list
```

### `omniglass action-rule optIn`

Opt yourself back in to a group notification

```
omniglass action-rule optIn <name>
```

Undoes your opt-out of a platform action rule; always allowed. Idempotent and audited. Gated by notification:subscribe.

Example:

```sh
omniglass action-rule optIn <name>
```

### `omniglass action-rule optOut`

Opt yourself out of a group notification

```
omniglass action-rule optOut <name>
```

Stops a platform action rule telling you through a group it targets, for you alone. Only a rule an admin marked opt_out_allowed (a 409 otherwise); a rule that names you directly still tells you. Idempotent and audited. Gated by notification:subscribe.

Example:

```sh
omniglass action-rule optOut <name>
```

### `omniglass action-rule update`

Update an action rule

```
omniglass action-rule update <name> [flags]
```

Patches a rule (an absent field is unchanged; on and targets replace their sets). It acts on transitions from the next one; a notification already queued is not re-rendered. Audited. Gated by rule:update, with an all-scope grant.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--description` | string | (none) | What it is for |
| `--enabled` | bool | `false` | Whether it fires: a disabled rule queues nothing on a transition, and what it queued before still delivers; re-enabled, it acts on the next transition |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A human label (empty clears it) |
| `--notification-type` | string | (none) | The type to send (empty returns to the official one per transition) |
| `--on` | string | (none) | The transitions it fires on (replaces the set) |
| `--opt-out-allowed` | bool | `false` | Let a member of a group it targets opt out of it; false withdraws every opt-out from the next transition |
| `--targets` | string | (none) | The targets (replaces the set) |
| `--when` | string | (none) | The predicate (empty always holds) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass action-rule update <name>
```

## `omniglass audit-log`

Commands for the audit-log resource

### `omniglass audit-log list`

List audit-trail events

```
omniglass audit-log list [flags]
```

Recent audit-trail events, newest first, each with the actor and, for an impersonated action, the real actor behind it. Read-only; gated by audit:read:admin (admin/owner only, since the audit trail is admin-sensitive).

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--before` | string | (none) | Only events strictly older than this RFC3339 timestamp (paging backward) |
| `--limit` | int | `0` | Max rows to return, newest first (default 100, capped at 500) |
| `--resource` | string | (none) | Filter to one resource kind (e.g. auth, principal_grant) |
| `--verb` | string | (none) | Filter to one verb (e.g. login, create) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass audit-log list
```

## `omniglass auth`

Commands for the auth resource

### `omniglass auth avatar`

Get your own profile picture

```
omniglass auth avatar
```

Returns the caller's profile picture as a base64-encoded JPEG. Requires authentication; self-scoped. No picture is a 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth avatar
```

### `omniglass auth change-password`

Change your own password

```
omniglass auth change-password [flags]
```

Verifies the current password and sets a new one. Requires authentication; self-scoped.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--current-password` | string | (none) | Your current password |
| `--new-password` | string | (none) | The new password (at least 12 characters, not a common password, not containing the username) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth change-password --current-password current_password --new-password new_password
```

### `omniglass auth create-token`

Create one of your own API tokens

```
omniglass auth create-token [flags]
```

Mints a CLI/API token for the caller and returns it once (store it now; it cannot be retrieved again). A description is required (what the token is for); an optional ttl_days bounds its lifetime (default 90, maximum 365). Requires authentication; self-scoped (always issued for you). The token is stamped with the device and address that created it.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--description` | string | (none) | What the token is for (required) |
| `--ttl-days` | int | `0` | Days until the token expires (default 90, maximum 365) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth create-token --description description
```

### `omniglass auth login`

Log in with a username and password

```
omniglass auth login [flags]
```

Verifies a human's password and sets an httpOnly session cookie. Public; a bad credential is a flat 401, and a correct password against a disabled account is a distinct 403 so the screen can explain it.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--password` | string | (none) | The account password; exchanged for a session cookie, never stored |
| `--username` | string | (none) | The sign-in username |

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth login --password password --username username
```

### `omniglass auth logout`

Log out the current session

```
omniglass auth logout
```

Revokes the session token and clears the cookie. Public.

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth logout
```

### `omniglass auth me`

The authenticated principal, its permissions, and grants

```
omniglass auth me [flags]
```

Returns the caller's principal, flattened permissions (a UI hint and the fast-reject set), the permissions held on an all-scope grant (fleet_permissions), and grants. Requires authentication.

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth me
```

#### `omniglass auth me action-rule`

Commands for the action-rule resource

##### `omniglass auth me action-rule create`

Subscribe yourself to alarms

```
omniglass auth me action-rule create [flags]
```

Creates a personal action rule: on which alarm transitions, when, what to send, and on which of your channels (inbox, email). It tells you alone and names no target (targets is a 422), and it only ever matches an alarm on a component you can read at that moment, judged before its when runs. A taken name among your rules, or a 51st rule, is a 409. Audited. Gated by notification:subscribe.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--channels` | string | (none) | How it tells you: inbox, email (your directory email) |
| `--description` | string | (none) | What it is for |
| `--enabled` | bool | `false` | Whether it fires (default true) |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A human label |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The rule's name (lowercase kebab), unique among your own rules |
| `--notification-type` | string | (none) | The notification type to send, by name or uuid; absent sends the official one for the transition |
| `--on` | string | (none) | The alarm transitions it fires on: raised, cleared, or both |
| `--targets` | string | (none) | Refused when set (a 422): a personal rule tells you alone and names no target |
| `--when` | string | (none) | A predicate over the alarm facts (component, place, severity, severity_rank, message, rule, ...); absent always holds. Judged only for alarms on components you can read |

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth me action-rule create --channels <json> --name name --on <json>
```

##### `omniglass auth me action-rule delete`

Unsubscribe: delete one of your alarm subscriptions

```
omniglass auth me action-rule delete <name>
```

Deletes one of your own personal action rules; what it already sent keeps its name. Another user's is a 404. Audited. Gated by notification:subscribe.

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth me action-rule delete <name>
```

Get one of your alarm subscriptions

```

```

One of your own personal action rules, by name or uuid; another user's is a 404. Gated by notification:subscribe.


List your alarm subscriptions

```

```

Your own personal action rules, by name. Self-scoped. Gated by notification:subscribe.

##### `omniglass auth me action-rule test`

Test one of your alarm subscriptions against your recent alarms

```
omniglass auth me action-rule test <name> [flags]
```

Judges one of your own personal action rules, or a draft of its on and when, against your most recent alarms on components you can read: for each transition it fires on, whether it would have told you. Writes and sends nothing. Another user's rule is a 404. Gated by notification:subscribe.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | int | `0` | How many of your most recent alarms to judge (default 20) |
| `--on` | string | (none) | A draft of the transitions to judge with, in place of the rule's own |
| `--when` | string | (none) | A draft of the predicate to judge with, in place of the rule's own |

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth me action-rule test <name>
```

##### `omniglass auth me action-rule testDraft`

Test a draft alarm subscription against your recent alarms

```
omniglass auth me action-rule testDraft [flags]
```

Judges a draft's on (default raised) and when (default always) against your most recent alarms on components you can read, before it is saved: for each transition, whether it would have told you. Writes and sends nothing. Gated by notification:subscribe.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | int | `0` | How many of your most recent alarms to judge (default 20) |
| `--on` | string | (none) | The transitions to judge (default raised) |
| `--when` | string | (none) | The predicate to judge (default always) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth me action-rule testDraft
```

Change or pause one of your alarm subscriptions

```

```

Patches one of your own personal action rules (an absent field is unchanged); enabled false pauses it. Another user's is a 404. Audited. Gated by notification:subscribe.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--channels` | string | (none) | How it tells you (replaces the set) |
| `--description` | string | (none) | What it is for |
| `--enabled` | bool | `false` | Whether it fires: false pauses it, true resumes it from the next transition |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A human label (empty clears it) |

| `--on` | string | (none) | The transitions it fires on (replaces the set) |
| `--when` | string | (none) | The predicate (empty always holds) |

Example:

#### `omniglass auth me notification`

Commands for the notification resource

##### `omniglass auth me notification list`

List your inbox

```
omniglass auth me notification list [flags]
```

The caller's own console inbox: the notifications addressed to them on the inbox channel, newest first, with the unread count. Self-scoped (never another principal's), and scoped again by the caller's component read scope as it stands now, so an entry about a component they can no longer read is gone. Gated by notification:read.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | int | `0` | At most this many, newest first (default 100) |
| `--unread` | bool | `false` | Only the entries not yet read |

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth me notification list
```

##### `omniglass auth me notification markAllRead`

Mark every inbox entry read

```
omniglass auth me notification markAllRead
```

Marks every unread entry in the caller's own inbox read, over the same scope the inbox reads, and says how many. Audited as one row. Gated by notification:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth me notification markAllRead
```

##### `omniglass auth me notification markRead`

Mark an inbox entry read

```
omniglass auth me notification markRead <id>
```

Marks one of the caller's own inbox entries read (one already read keeps its first read time). An entry that is not the caller's, or about a component outside their component read scope, is a non-disclosing 404. Audited. Gated by notification:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass auth me notification markRead <id>
```

## `omniglass calc-rule`

Commands for the calc-rule resource

### `omniglass calc-rule create`

Create a calc rule

```
omniglass calc-rule create [flags]
```

Authors a rule that derives its output key on each owner (each component its selector picks, or each system) from its aliased inputs, reduced by an expression over the aliases, each bound as the list of its current values (one per instance on a component, every member's on a system, with members records beside it). Every input key must be registered (by name or uuid; the rule holds it by uuid) and health may not be one; each alias is an identifier of at most 64, not a keyword, a builtin or list function's name, or a site binding (component, has, members, system, value), and unique; the reduce must compile and yield the output key's type (a 422 placed at body.reduce.expr with its line and column, and the name when it is one no alias binds); the output must be a registered key that is not health and that no collection writes (a native probe's key, or one a driver declares among its emits); an enabled rule may not close a cycle in the graph from every enabled rule's input keys to its output key (a 422 naming the chain of keys), nor write a key another enabled rule writes (a 422 naming that rule). A list or get carries calc_error when a stored reduce no longer compiles. A name already taken is a 409. Returns the rule with its uuid. Audited. Gated by rule:create, with an all-scope grant.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--description` | string | (none) | What the rule derives and why |
| `--enabled` | bool | `false` | Defaults to true |
| `--inputs` | string | (none) | The keys the rule reads, each by a unique alias its reduce uses; health may not be one |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A human label |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The rule's name (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens) |
| `--output-key` | string | (none) | The property or metric the rule writes: its type pins the reduce's result. Not a reserved key (a native probe key, health), not a key a driver's emits or a command type write, and not one another enabled rule writes |
| `--owner-kind` | string | (none) | What the rule derives a value on: each component its selector picks, or each system its selector picks (read from the system's role-bound members). Fixed at create |
| `--reduce` | string | (none) | An expression over the inputs by alias |
| `--selector` | string | (none) | The owners the rule derives for: a component rule's component_types and components, or a system rule's system_types and systems; absent is every owner of its kind |

Example:

```sh
omniglass calc-rule create --inputs <json> --name name --output-key output_key --owner-kind owner_kind --reduce <json>
```

### `omniglass calc-rule delete`

Delete a calc rule

```
omniglass calc-rule delete <name>
```

Removes an operator rule; an official rule is read-only (409). Audited. Gated by rule:delete, with an all-scope grant.

Example:

```sh
omniglass calc-rule delete <name>
```

### `omniglass calc-rule get`

Get a calc rule

```
omniglass calc-rule get <name>
```

Returns one calc rule by name (or uuid). Gated by rule:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass calc-rule get <name>
```

### `omniglass calc-rule list`

List calc rules

```
omniglass calc-rule list
```

Lists the calc rules, by name: the authored config that derives an output key on each owner from aliased inputs, each with its live state as counts (owners_computed, owners_pending, owners_unsupported, owners_failed) over the owners the caller may read. Rules read like a registry, so every rule is listed whatever the caller's scope. Gated by rule:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass calc-rule list
```

### `omniglass calc-rule preview`

Preview a calc rule

```
omniglass calc-rule preview [flags]
```

Computes a candidate calc rule now, on each owner it selects that the caller may read, with the reduce the tick runs, and writes nothing (a read-only transaction). For each owner it answers the value the rule would write, the output's current value and whether they differ, the inputs with no value, the members skipped and the instances left out as stale (named when the caller may read the component, else counted). An expression that reads one member's value by position (members[1].value.t, or an element of an input's list) over a system with a member the caller may not read is withheld on that system, its error counting the members out of scope; one that folds each input's list whole (avg(t), max(t)) shows the aggregate. A component rule previews the selected components holding one of its inputs, as the tick would mark them. The owners holding a current value of the output are computed first, so the cap never hides one, and the answer lists the owners holding a value or that the rule would write one on first, each by name. At most owner_cap owners are computed, and a bound on total input reads stops a preview over large systems early, a whole owner at a time (owners_judged of owners_total, truncated past either). The candidate is checked as a save would check it: a reduce that does not compile, a cycle in the key graph, an output another enabled rule or a collection writes, or health are each a 422, so the author learns before saving; given a saved rule's name it is judged as an edit of that rule. The selector's names resolve in the caller's read scope: a name that does not exist and one the caller may not read are the same 422, and a name shared in and out of scope means the one in scope. A preview takes no lock a save waits on. Gated by rule:read.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--inputs` | string | (none) | The keys the rule reads, each by a unique alias its reduce uses |
| `--name` | string | (none) | A saved rule's name, to preview an edit of it (its stored version is then not a second writer of its key); absent for a new rule |
| `--output-key` | string | (none) | The property or metric the rule would write |
| `--owner-kind` | string | (none) | What the rule derives a value on |
| `--reduce` | string | (none) | An expression over the inputs by alias |
| `--selector` | string | (none) | The owners the rule derives for; absent is every owner of its kind |

Example:

```sh
omniglass calc-rule preview --inputs <json> --output-key output_key --owner-kind owner_kind --reduce <json>
```

### `omniglass calc-rule rename`

Rename a calc rule

```
omniglass calc-rule rename <name> [flags]
```

Moves an operator rule's name, the address an operator types. A separate act from an update, because it breaks bookmarks and integration config outside this system; inside it nothing breaks, since the audit rows hold the rule's uuid and the key graph is of keys, not rule names. Not a material change: no version bump. An official rule keeps its name (409), a taken name is a 409, an illegal or uuid-shaped one a 422. Returns the rule with its uuid. Audited. Gated by rule:update, with an all-scope grant.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name` | string | (none) | The rule's new name, unique among calc rules (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass calc-rule rename <name> --name name
```

### `omniglass calc-rule state`

Commands for the state resource

#### `omniglass calc-rule state list`

Get a calc rule's live state

```
omniglass calc-rule state list <name> [flags]
```

What a calc rule last did on each owner the caller may read (components by the component read scope, systems by the system read scope), each owner named now: the value it computed, when and at which version, the inputs it found no value of, a system's members that held none and the instances it left out as stale (named when the caller may read the component, else counted), an error, since when a system has had no members, and whether the owner is pending (with when a deferred mark is due). Ordered on the server, failing owners first, then pending, then those it wrote nothing for, then those holding a value, each by name, and at most limit of them; total and the pending depth count every owner the caller may read, listed or not. Gated by rule:read.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | int | `0` | The most owners to list, in state order: failing, pending, missing an input (or with no members), valued, each by name |

Example:

```sh
omniglass calc-rule state list <name>
```

### `omniglass calc-rule update`

Update a calc rule

```
omniglass calc-rule update <name> [flags]
```

Patches a rule (an absent field is unchanged), bumping its version; a patch that changes nothing writes nothing. What changed is checked as on create: changed inputs, reduce or output recompile, a changed output must be one no collection writes, and an enabled rule may not close a cycle or share its output with another enabled rule. Enabling a disabled rule recompiles it and checks both, so a rule carrying calc_error cannot be enabled (422). The owner kind is fixed at create. Official rules are read-only (409). Audited. Gated by rule:update, with an all-scope grant.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--description` | string | (none) | What the rule derives and why |
| `--enabled` | bool | `false` | Whether the rule runs; an enabled rule is part of the key graph |
| `--inputs` | string | (none) | Replace the keys the rule reads |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A human label |
| `--output-key` | string | (none) | The property or metric the rule writes |
| `--reduce` | string | (none) | Replace the reduce's expression |
| `--selector` | string | (none) | Replace the owners the rule derives for; an empty selector is every owner of its kind |

Example:

```sh
omniglass calc-rule update <name>
```

## `omniglass command-type`

Commands for the command-type resource

### `omniglass command-type create`

Create a command type

```
omniglass command-type create [flags]
```

Registers a custom command type (official=false). The name must be a single kebab token; a target, when set, must be a registered property or metric type. Gated by command_type:create.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--description` | string | (none) | What the command does |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A human label |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The command type name (lowercase kebab) |
| `--params-schema` | string | (none) | A JSON Schema fragment for the params |
| `--settle-window-seconds` | int | `0` | The actuation window in seconds: how long the device is given to actuate before a mismatch is a failed command. 0 means settle immediately (a fire-and-forget command, or a settleable one judged at the moment of issue). A duration has no negative, so the schema floors it at 0 rather than accepting a value that behaves as 0 with no refusal to say so. |
| `--target-metric-type` | string | (none) | The metric this command sets, for settlement (at most one target arm) |
| `--target-property-type` | string | (none) | The property this command sets, for settlement (at most one target arm) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass command-type create --name name
```

### `omniglass command-type delete`

Delete a command type

```
omniglass command-type delete <name>
```

Removes a custom command type by name. Official types are read-only. Gated by command_type:delete.

Example:

```sh
omniglass command-type delete <name>
```

### `omniglass command-type get`

Get a command type

```
omniglass command-type get <name>
```

Returns one command type by name. Gated by command_type:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass command-type get <name>
```

### `omniglass command-type list`

List command types

```
omniglass command-type list
```

Lists every registered command type (official and custom). Fleet-wide reference data. Gated by command_type:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass command-type list
```

### `omniglass command-type update`

Update a command type

```
omniglass command-type update <name> [flags]
```

Patches a custom command type's label, description, params schema, settle window, or target on either arm (a nil field is unchanged; an empty target clears it; a non-empty arm clears the other). The name is fixed at creation. Official types are read-only. Gated by command_type:update.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--description` | string | (none) | What the command does |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A human label |
| `--params-schema` | string | (none) | A JSON Schema fragment (replaces wholesale) |
| `--settle-window-seconds` | int | `0` | The actuation window in seconds, floored at 0 (a duration has no negative; 0 means settle immediately) |
| `--target-metric-type` | string | (none) | The metric this command sets (empty clears it; a non-empty arm clears the other) |
| `--target-property-type` | string | (none) | The property this command sets (empty clears it; a non-empty arm clears the other) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass command-type update <name>
```

## `omniglass component`

Commands for the component resource

### `omniglass component alarm`

Commands for the alarm resource

#### `omniglass component alarm acknowledge`

Acknowledge an alarm

```
omniglass component alarm acknowledge <name> <id>
```

Records that a human has seen this alarm, and changes nothing else. The alarm stays exactly as raised as it was: acknowledging is not fixing, so health is NOT recomputed and cleared_at is untouched. Acknowledging is orthogonal to clearing in both directions, so a cleared alarm can still be acknowledged by whoever reviews the history, and clearing never acknowledges on an operator's behalf. Acknowledging twice is idempotent: the first person and the first time stay, and the no-op writes no second audit row. Gated by alarm:acknowledge, whose scope is resolved on the component tier from that permission (not from component:update); a component outside the caller's component:read is a non-disclosing 404, and one it can read but not acknowledge on is a 403.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component alarm acknowledge <name> <id>
```

#### `omniglass component alarm create`

Raise an alarm on a component

```
omniglass component alarm create <name> [flags]
```

Records a condition on this component, then recomputes health in the same transaction: the component's own verdict moves, and if it is now outage (an alarm at or above the high level), any role it occupies loses it as an occupant while the alarm is active, which can move its system and location verdicts with it; a lesser alarm degrades the component but leaves it occupying its roles. Gated by component:update; read and update scopes drive the 404 versus 403 split.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--dedup-key` | string | (none) | The condition identity; defaults to the message. Raising an already-open (component, dedup_key) returns the existing open alarm instead of a duplicate. A key (or, without one, a message) beginning rule: is refused (422): that namespace names a rule's condition |
| `--message` | string | (none) | What is wrong, for the operator reading it later |
| `--severity` | string | (none) | How bad it is: a severity level by name (see /severity-levels); a level at or above high puts the component itself in outage |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component alarm create <name> --severity severity
```

#### `omniglass component alarm delete`

Clear an alarm

```
omniglass component alarm delete <name> <id>
```

Marks the alarm cleared and recomputes health in the same transaction, so the recovery is recorded as a transition at the moment it happened. The row is kept: what was wrong and when outlives the fix. Clearing an alarm that is already cleared or does not exist is a 404. Gated by component:update; read and update scopes drive the 404 versus 403 split.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component alarm delete <name> <id>
```

#### `omniglass component alarm list`

List a component's alarms

```
omniglass component alarm list <name> [flags]
```

What is currently wrong with this component, newest first, with the component's own verdict those alarms make. Pass include_cleared for the history rather than the active set. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--include-cleared` | bool | `false` | Include cleared alarms, so the list is the history rather than what is wrong now |
| `--unacknowledged` | bool | `false` | Only the alarms nobody has looked at. On its own this is the queue an operator works (raised and unacknowledged); with include_cleared it also returns the incidents that came and went unattended |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component alarm list <name>
```

#### `omniglass component alarm snooze`

Snooze an alarm's condition

```
omniglass component alarm snooze <name> <id> [flags]
```

Snoozes the alarm's condition, its component and dedup_key, for a duration from now (1m to 7d), so every notification any alarm of that condition would send, a raise or a clear, on any channel, is written suppressed with the reason instead, and a message already waiting to be retried is suppressed when its turn comes. Snoozing a snoozed condition replaces the deadline. It changes nothing else: it does not acknowledge, does not recompute health, a snoozed alarm stays in the unacknowledged queue, and a clear does not end it. It notifies nothing itself. When the snooze ends, at its deadline or by :unsnooze, with an alarm of the condition still raised, that alarm is announced again as raised to whoever the action rules reach then. Audited on this alarm. Gated by alarm:snooze, whose scope is resolved on the component tier from that permission; a component outside the caller's component:read is a non-disclosing 404, and one it can read but not snooze on is a 403.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--duration` | string | (none) | How long from now the condition stays snoozed, from 1m to 7d: a duration such as 15m, 1h, 4h or 24h, or whole days such as 7d. Snoozing a snoozed condition replaces its deadline, shorter or longer |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component alarm snooze <name> <id> --duration duration
```

#### `omniglass component alarm timeline`

Read an alarm's timeline

```
omniglass component alarm timeline <name> <id>
```

The alarm's history in one list, oldest first: the events that carry it (an event rule's fire event, which opened it, and its clear event, which resolved it) merged by time with its audit rows (the raise, each acknowledgement, the clear, each snooze, unsnooze and snooze-end, and a rule edit that opened or resolved it, naming the editor) and the notifications its transitions queued, each at the moment it was queued with its status as it stands (#618). At one instant an event comes before the audit row it caused, and that before a notification. Gated by alarm:read; a component outside the caller's component read scope, and an alarm not on the component, are a non-disclosing 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component alarm timeline <name> <id>
```

#### `omniglass component alarm unsnooze`

End an alarm's condition's snooze

```
omniglass component alarm unsnooze <name> <id>
```

Ends the snooze on the alarm's condition early, exactly as its deadline passing would: if an alarm of the condition is still raised, it is announced again as raised to whoever the action rules reach now. Audited on this alarm, naming the caller. Unsnoozing a condition that is not snoozed is a 200 that writes nothing. Gated by alarm:snooze, resolved as :snooze is.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component alarm unsnooze <name> <id>
```

### `omniglass component checkName`

Check a component name

```
omniglass component checkName [flags]
```

Reports whether a proposed name is a valid slug and currently free within the given placement (parent wins over location; neither means the unplaced/root bucket). Advisory (Save is still gated by the unique constraint). Gated by component:update.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--location` | string | (none) | The location (by name or uuid) the entity would be placed at, if any and if unparented; ignored by the locations check |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The proposed name to check |
| `--parent` | string | (none) | The parent (by name or uuid) the entity would be created under, if any; omit for a root/unplaced check |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component checkName --name name
```

### `omniglass component command`

Commands for the command resource

#### `omniglass component command get`

Read a command

```
omniglass component command get <name> <id>
```

One command, whole: what it was told and the value it set, its recorded status with a time for each transition (issued, delivered, executed, settled), where it sits now while in flight (queued, delivered, awaiting the reply, awaiting the observation), how its binding settles it, the evidence that decided it (the reply, masked of credentials, or the observed sample) and why, the endpoint, node and driver that carry it, and who issued it. Gated by command:read, resolved on the component tier; a component outside the caller's component:read, or a command not on that component, is a non-disclosing 404, and a component it can read but whose commands it may not is a 403.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component command get 'hq.west.level-2.boardroom-a.$comp.videobar-1' 42
```

#### `omniglass component command issue`

Issue a command to a component

```
omniglass component command issue <name> [flags]
```

Records a command invocation, writes a caused event, and (for a settleable command) opens an intended value the observed value settles against. Answers with the command as it stands (as the command read returns it) and the computed settlement verdict; with wait, once it settles, fails or times out, or wait_timeout passes. Gated by command:issue, whose scope is resolved on the component tier from that permission (not from component:read); a component outside the caller's component:read is a non-disclosing 404, and one it can read but not command is a 403.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--command-type` | string | (none) | The command_type to invoke |
| `--instance` | string | (none) | The series discriminator (e.g. an endpoint), when the target is instanced |
| `--params` | string | (none) | The invocation params, stored on the command and the caused event |
| `--value` | string | (none) | The intended value for the target property (a settleable command) |
| `--wait` | bool | `false` | Block until the command settles, fails or times out, or until wait_timeout passes, and answer with where it stands then. Refused with a 429, before anything is issued, while too many commands are already being waited on |
| `--wait-timeout` | int | `0` | How long a wait may block, in seconds (1 to 120). A command still in flight when it passes is answered as it stands, its phase saying where |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component command issue <name> --command-type command_type
```

#### `omniglass component command list`

List a component's commands

```
omniglass component command list <name> [flags]
```

The component's command history, newest first, each command whole (as the single read returns it), narrowed by recorded status and by when it was issued, a page at a time. status=issued is what is in flight now. Gated by command:read, resolved on the component tier; a component outside the caller's component:read is a non-disclosing 404, and one it can read but whose commands it may not is a 403.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--limit` | int | `0` | How many to return, newest first (1 to 500) |
| `--since` | string | (none) | Only the commands issued at or after this RFC3339 time |
| `--status` | string | (none) | Only the commands with this recorded status; issued is every command still in flight |
| `--until` | string | (none) | Only the commands issued at or before this RFC3339 time |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component command list 'hq.west.level-2.boardroom-a.$comp.videobar-1'
```

### `omniglass component create`

Create a component

```
omniglass component create [flags]
```

Creates a component, optionally under a parent (a root needs an all-scoped grant), bound to a system and a location, and classified by a product (required; naming a generic is fine until a real product is modeled). Gated by component:create. The location reference resolves within the caller's location:read scope, because the label this stores is rendered from it, and one outside that scope is refused (422) exactly as :renderLabel refuses to preview it. Naming a system additionally requires system:update, and resolves within that scope, because the component's primary membership is inserted from it: it is the same row the membership route writes, so the two paths cost the same permission. A system outside that scope is refused with a 403 naming it when the caller may read the system (denying its existence to someone who can GET it would be a lie) and with the non-disclosing 422 when the caller may not.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--expected-name` | string | (none) | The name a create form previewed (POST /components:renderLabel returns it). The create is refused with a 409 naming what it would produce instead, rather than silently landing a different name, if the number was taken or the type's stem moved while the form was open. It does not name the row (the platform still does, and the row is still name_generated): it only asserts what that name will be. Applies only when the platform names the row: sending it beside a name is a 422. |
| `--label` | string | (none) | What an operator reads; the name is the address |
| `--location` | string | (none) | Location name this component is placed at |
| `--name` | string | (none) | Name, unique within its placement (the address; lowercase letters, digits, hyphens). Omit to have the platform generate one from the product's type. |
| `--parent` | string | (none) | Parent component name; omit for a root component |
| `--product` | string | (none) | Product (catalog SKU) this component is an instance of, by name or uuid. Required: use a generic (generic-device, generic-app, generic-service) until a real product is modeled. |
| `--system` | string | (none) | Primary system name this component belongs to. Naming one writes that system's membership, so it costs the system:update permission and resolves in that scope; omitted, the create costs component:create alone. |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component create
```

### `omniglass component createFromTemplate`

Start a component from a template

```
omniglass component createFromTemplate [flags]
```

Creates one component from a component template at a place: its product and the template's declared values, and, when the inputs carry an address (host), its endpoint attached through the driver with the template's preset under your inputs. A secret input names a secret you may read, resolved as an attach resolves it. One transaction, every piece in your own scope with its own audit row carrying from_template; nothing points back at the template. Gated by component:create; declared values also need component:update and an attach endpoint:create. A place outside your location scope is a 404, an unknown template a 404, inputs with no address or an attach with no node a 422.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--inputs` | string | (none) | Driver inputs laid over the template's preset: the address (host) attaches the endpoint, a secret input names a secret you may read |
| `--label` | string | (none) | The component's label |
| `--location` | string | (none) | The place the component sits in, by name or dotted path |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The component's name; minted as an unnamed create mints it when empty |
| `--node` | string | (none) | The node the endpoint is placed on; needed when inputs carry an address |
| `--template` | string | (none) | The component template, by name |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component createFromTemplate --template template
```

### `omniglass component delete`

Delete a component

```
omniglass component delete <name>
```

Deletes a component, refused (409) while it still has child components or is still referenced elsewhere, such as by a system role it staffs. Gated by component:delete; read and delete scopes drive the 404 versus 403 split.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component delete <name>
```

### `omniglass component effective-secret`

Commands for the effective-secret resource

#### `omniglass component effective-secret list`

Effective secrets for a component

```
omniglass component effective-secret list <name>
```

Resolves the secrets that cascade onto a component (platform -> location -> component), with the winner and the shadowed candidates it overrode. There is NO system band: a secret is device-facing, and the room a component happens to serve is the wrong owner for a credential the device itself answers with. Fields are masked, as in the directory; plaintext is only ever the audited reveal. Gated by secret:read, which the viewer floor does not carry, and admin-sensitive secrets appear only to the admin tier.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component effective-secret list <name>
```

### `omniglass component effective-tag`

Commands for the effective-tag resource

#### `omniglass component effective-tag list`

Effective tags for a component

```
omniglass component effective-tag list <name> [flags]
```

Resolves the tags that cascade onto a component (platform -> location -> system -> component): keys union, values override most-specific-wins, with the winner and shadowed candidates. A non-propagating key resolves only from a binding on the component itself. The system band comes from MEMBERSHIP: pass ?system= (a name or a uuid, ADR-0062) to resolve against one the component belongs to (a shared device answers differently for each), or omit it to resolve against its primary membership. Gated by component:read; the component must be in the caller's component read scope.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--system` | string | (none) | Resolve against this system, name or uuid (ADR-0062), which the component must be a member of. Omit to resolve against its primary membership, the default for a caller with no system in hand. |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component effective-tag list <name>
```

### `omniglass component effective-variable`

Commands for the effective-variable resource

#### `omniglass component effective-variable list`

Effective variables for a component

```
omniglass component effective-variable list <name>
```

Resolves the variables that cascade onto a component (platform -> location -> system -> component): names union, values override most-specific-wins, with the winner and the shadowed candidates it overrode. The system band comes from the component's PRIMARY membership; resolving against a named system is not offered here yet, unlike effective-tags. Gated by variable:read; the component must be in the caller's component read scope.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component effective-variable list <name>
```

### `omniglass component event`

Commands for the event resource

#### `omniglass component event list`

List a component's recent events

```
omniglass component event list <name>
```

Returns the component's recent log occurrences (the log-kind sink), newest first, bounded to the last 24 hours. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component event list <name>
```

### `omniglass component get`

Get a component

```
omniglass component get <name>
```

Fetches a component by name within the caller's read scope. Out of scope is a non-disclosing 404. Gated by component:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component get <name>
```

### `omniglass component identity-binding`

Commands for the identity-binding resource

#### `omniglass component identity-binding delete`

Unbind an identity a conduit reports

```
omniglass component identity-binding delete <name> <key> <value>
```

Removes the binding of this value, reported by the conduit component under this match key, so its samples no longer land on the owner it named. Unbinding writes onto both ends, so it costs a write on both: gated by component:update on the conduit, and it also needs update on the binding's owner (component:update, or system:update for a system), a 403 naming it when the caller reads the owner but cannot write it. A binding whose owner the caller cannot read is a 404, as one that does not exist is: the list does not name it either.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component identity-binding delete ucc-service-1 ucc-room-id room-17c-415a
```

#### `omniglass component identity-binding list`

List the identities a conduit component fans out

```
omniglass component identity-binding list <name>
```

The identity bindings of this conduit component: each value it reports under a match key (a registered property type, such as ucc-room-id) and the one system or component that value's samples land on. A component that speaks for many owners (a cloud service, a controller fronting many components) is the conduit, the path rather than the owner. Each binding is named only when its owner is inside the caller's read on its tier (system:read for a system owner, component:read for a component owner); the rest are counted in hidden, never named. Gated by component:read; a conduit outside it is a non-disclosing 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component identity-binding list ucc-service-1
```

#### `omniglass component identity-binding update`

Bind an identity a conduit reports to its owner

```
omniglass component identity-binding update <name> <key> <value> [flags]
```

Ties this value, reported by the conduit component under this match key, to one owner, a system or a component, so the conduit's samples naming it land on that owner. One identity on one conduit has exactly one owner: a put naming the owner it is already bound to changes nothing, and one naming a different owner moves it. The match key must be a registered property type (422 otherwise), and the owner a component or a system other than the conduit itself (a place or a node owns no observed sample, and a value with no identity already lands on the conduit: each a 422). The value rides the path as one percent-encoded segment, so a value carrying a slash, a space or another reserved character is escaped (room%2F1) and round-trips. A binding writes onto both of its ends, so it costs a write on both: gated by component:update on the conduit, and it also needs the owner's update (component:update, or system:update for a system, refused with a 403 naming it before anything resolves). Each end resolves in its own tier's read scope and must be inside its update scope: an end outside the read scope is a non-disclosing 404, one readable but not writable a 403. A move also needs update on the owner it leaves; refused, it says the identity is bound to another owner but never which one.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--owner` | string | (none) | Name or uuid of the owner the identity's values land on, or a dotted address |
| `--owner-kind` | string | (none) | What kind of owner the identity names. A component or a system; a place or a node owns no observed sample, so neither is an owner here |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component identity-binding update ucc-service-1 ucc-room-id room-17c-415a --owner owner --owner-kind owner_kind
```

### `omniglass component impairment`

Commands for the impairment resource

#### `omniglass component impairment get`

Get what is broken on a simulated device

```
omniglass component impairment get <name>
```

The impairment an operator set on a simulated component (unplugged, or a degraded link), applied by the simulator beside its node when that simulator runs with impairments and NET_ADMIN. A healthy device reads all zero. Gated by simulation:read; the component resolves within the caller's component read scope.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component impairment get <name>
```

#### `omniglass component impairment set`

Break or repair a simulated device

```
omniglass component impairment set <name> [flags]
```

Sets what is broken on a simulated component: unplugged, or a link with added latency, jitter, loss or a rate limit. It replaces the whole impairment, so a field left out reads as zero (setting a latency on an unplugged device plugs it back in); an empty body repairs it. Returns the impairment as stored, loss rounded to hundredths. Audited. The simulator beside the component's node applies it on its next pull. Gated by simulation:update, whose scope is resolved on the component tier; a component outside the caller's component:read is a non-disclosing 404, and one it can read but not impair is a 403. Jitter above latency, or a value outside its range, is a 422.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--jitter-ms` | int | `0` | Variation on the delay, in milliseconds; at most the latency |
| `--latency-ms` | int | `0` | Delay added to traffic toward the device, in milliseconds |
| `--loss-pct` | float64 | `0` | Share of packets toward the device dropped, in percent, to hundredths |
| `--rate-kbit` | int | `0` | Bandwidth limit on the device's link, both ways, in kilobits per second; 0 is unlimited |
| `--unplugged` | bool | `false` | Dark on every protocol: connects time out, datagrams and pings go unanswered |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component impairment set <name>
```

List components in scope

```
omniglass component list
```

Lists the components the caller may read, each filtered to its scope subtree. Gated by component:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component list
```

### `omniglass component listTags`

List tags on a component

```
omniglass component listTags <name>
```

Lists the tags bound directly on a component (not the resolved cascade). Gated by component:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component listTags <name>
```

### `omniglass component log`

Commands for the log resource

#### `omniglass component log list`

List a component's recent log lines

```
omniglass component log list <name> [flags]
```

Returns the component's recent raw log lines (the ingest lane of ADR-0066, distinct from typed events), newest first, bounded to the last 24 hours, narrowed by an optional severity threshold and source, with the sources the window carries. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--severity` | string | (none) | Only lines at this severity or more severe (RFC 5424's eight levels); a line with no severity is left out |
| `--source` | string | (none) | Only lines that arrived on this channel |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component log list <name>
```

### `omniglass component membership`

Commands for the membership resource

#### `omniglass component membership list`

List the systems a component is in

```

```

The systems this component is bound into, ordered by name. A component may belong to several: a rack DSP serving three rooms is a member of all three, and each of them depends on it. Exactly one membership may be marked primary, the default for a question asked without a system in hand. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component membership list <name>
```

### `omniglass component metric`

Commands for the metric resource

#### `omniglass component metric list`

List a component's effective metrics

```
omniglass component metric list <name>
```

Every metric the component's product declares, resolved to the newest observed or calculated sample across its live instances (instance names the one shown, instance_count counts them) or the contract default until one arrives (is_sampled marks a live series), plus any metric sampled directly on the component (from_contract false). Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component metric list <name>
```

#### `omniglass component metric sample`

Commands for the sample resource

##### `omniglass component metric sample list`

Read one metric series' raw samples

```
omniglass component metric sample list <name> <metric> [flags]
```

The samples behind the effective read's latest value for one series, newest first, windowed (hours) and capped (limit, newest kept). Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope owner is a non-disclosing 404.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--hours` | int | `0` | The window in hours, counted back from now; 24 when unset |
| `--limit` | int | `0` | The row cap, newest kept; 500 when unset |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component metric sample list <name> <metric>
```

### `omniglass component move`

Move a component

```
omniglass component move <name> [flags]
```

Relocates and/or re-parents a component: at least one of location or parent is required (422 otherwise). Both follow the three-state convention (an omitted field is unchanged, an explicit empty string clears, a name sets). A reparent is cycle-guarded and scope-injected; clearing parent to root requires an all-scoped move grant, the same authorization a root create already requires. A separate act from update, and a separately grantable one (component:move), because a placement change is an authorization act, not a label edit: it moves a row out from under one grant's subtree and under another's. Recorded under its own audit verb, move, distinct from update. Does not recompute health: a component's own verdict is purely its active alarms, unaffected by where it sits. A taken name at the destination is a 409. Gated by component:move; read and move scopes drive the 404 versus 403 split, and the destination location resolves within the caller's location:read scope, because the move restamps the label from it: a destination outside that scope is refused (422).

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--location` | string | (none) | Relocates the component to this location name. An empty string clears its placement. |
| `--parent` | string | (none) | Re-parents the component within the component tree to this component name; cycle-guarded and scope-injected. An empty string makes it a root component (requires an all-scoped move grant). |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component move <name>
```

### `omniglass component previewLabels`

Preview a component label recompute

```
omniglass component previewLabels
```

Lists exactly the rows a recompute would change, and leaves the fleet as it found it. Use it before :recomputeLabels to see the blast radius of a rule edit. Every generated label in the caller's read and update scope is re-rendered from its current rules and compared with what is stored; a label an operator typed by hand is never a candidate. Bounded by the same two scopes the apply is, so it never lists a row the apply would then refuse to touch. A location preview also lists the components and systems placed at every location whose label would move, because those go stale the moment it does. Gated by component:update, the same permission the apply needs: a preview is half of an edit rather than a report, and an operator who cannot apply has no use for it.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component previewLabels
```

### `omniglass component property`

Commands for the property resource

#### `omniglass component property delete`

Clear a property on a component

```
omniglass component property delete <name> <property>
```

Removes the component's declared value, so the property falls back to the product contract's default (or leaves the effective read entirely when it was off-contract). Clearing a property the component never set is a 404. Gated by component:update; read and update scopes drive the 404 versus 403 split.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component property delete <name> <property>
```

#### `omniglass component property list`

List a component's properties and where each stands

```
omniglass component property list <name>
```

Every property the component has: each its product declares, resolved to the component's own value or the contract default (is_set marks the override), each set directly on the component (from_contract false), each a calc rule writes (source_rule), and each only observed or told by a command. Every row but a calculated one carries its reconciliation: want (declared), told (intended), is (observed, worst case across every live instance, naming is_instance) and drift, computed on read. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component property list <name>
```

#### `omniglass component property sample`

Commands for the sample resource

##### `omniglass component property sample list`

Read one property series' change history

```
omniglass component property sample list <name> <property> [flags]
```

The change history behind the effective value for one property series, newest first, windowed (hours) and capped (limit, newest kept). Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope owner is a non-disclosing 404.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--hours` | int | `0` | The window in hours, counted back from now; 24 when unset |
| `--limit` | int | `0` | The row cap, newest kept; 500 when unset |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component property sample list <name> <property>
```

#### `omniglass component property update`

Set a property on a component

```
omniglass component property update <name> <property> [flags]
```

Declares a value for the property on this component, overriding the product contract's default. Idempotent: the first set stores the value, a later set replaces it. The property need not be on the contract, but it must exist in the catalog (422 otherwise). Gated by component:update; read and update scopes drive the 404 versus 403 split.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--value` | string | (none) | The value to declare, shape given by the property's data_type |

### `omniglass component reachability`

Commands for the reachability resource

#### `omniglass component reachability list`

Read a component's per-endpoint reachability

```
omniglass component reachability list <name>
```

Composes, per endpoint, the latest reachability verdict, the probe-layer signals that compose it, and the recent verdict transitions for the availability strip. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope component is a non-disclosing 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component reachability list <name>
```

### `omniglass component recomputeLabels`

Recompute component labels

```
omniglass component recomputeLabels
```

Applies what :previewLabels describes, over the rows in the caller's read and update scope, and returns exactly what it changed. Idempotent: a second call changes nothing. A label an operator typed by hand is left alone, and clearing that label by hand is how it is handed back to the platform. Recorded as ONE audit row for the operation, naming the rule tier and the affected count, rather than one row per changed entity. Gated by component:update.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component recomputeLabels
```

### `omniglass component removeTag`

Remove a tag value from a component

```
omniglass component removeTag <name> [flags]
```

Removes a key's value from a component. Gated by component:update.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key` | string | (none) | The tag key to remove |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component removeTag <name> --key key
```

### `omniglass component rename`

Rename a component

```
omniglass component rename <name> [flags]
```

Moves the component's name, the address an operator types and every external reference stores. A separate act from an update, and a separately grantable one, because it breaks bookmarks, runbooks, and integration config outside this system; inside it nothing breaks, since every reference holds the uuid. A taken name is a 409, an illegal or uuid-shaped one a 422. Gated by component:rename; read and rename scopes drive the 404 versus 403 split.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--name` | string | (none) | The new name, unique within its placement (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens) |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component rename <name> --name name
```

### `omniglass component renderLabel`

Draft the name and label a component create would store

```
omniglass component renderLabel [flags]
```

Drafts the name and the label a component create would stamp, for the classification and placement a create form already holds, without creating anything. It allocates no ordinal, opens no write transaction and takes no advisory lock, which is what separates it from a preview that mints: the ordinal is READ (the lowest free number among the live siblings in the placement bucket) rather than allocated. That answer is provisional, so a form posts the NAME back as expected_name on the create and is refused (409) rather than silently renamed if another create takes the number or the type's stem moves first. Omitting name drafts the name the platform would mint, and refuses (422) exactly where a nameless create would. Gated by component:create, the permission the create it precedes needs; the parent resolves within the caller's component:create scope and the location ref within location:read, because the rendered string can carry that label. Naming a system additionally requires system:update and resolves within that scope, the same as the create, because the create binds that system's membership: a preview is never served for a bind the create would refuse. Omitting parent is the parentless bucket, which a create refuses without an all-scoped grant, so the draft refuses it too (403): a form must not preview a bucket its create declines, and the previewed ordinal reports which names that bucket already holds.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--location` | string | (none) | The location this component will sit at, by name or uuid. Resolved within the caller's location:read scope: a location out of scope is refused, never rendered. |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The name the row will carry. Omit it to draft the name and label the platform would produce; supply it to draft the label an operator-named row would carry, which has no ordinal at all. |
| `--parent` | string | (none) | The parent component, by name or uuid. Part of the placement bucket a generated name's ordinal is read from, so a draft that omits it previews the wrong bucket. Resolved within the caller's component:create scope, the same set the create resolves it in. |
| `--product` | string | (none) | The product this component is an instance of, by name or uuid; the classification both a label rule and a generated name are resolved from |
| `--system` | string | (none) | The system this component will belong to, by name or uuid. Naming it requires system:update, exactly as the create does, because the create inserts that system's membership; it resolves within that scope, and system:read decides only whether the refusal may name the system. |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component renderLabel --product product
```

### `omniglass component resetName`

Regenerate a component's name

```
omniglass component resetName <name>
```

Hands the pen back to the platform: regenerates the name from the component's current type and placement (the same "<stem>-<n>" rule a nameless create applies) and marks it name_generated, whether or not it already was. Gated by component:rename, the same token :rename uses: it changes the name, exactly that permission's blast radius.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component resetName <name>
```

### `omniglass component setTag`

Set a tag value on a component

```
omniglass component setTag <name> [flags]
```

Binds a value for a key on a component. The key must exist and apply to this entity kind. Setting a value is the ordinary entity write, gated by component:update.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--key` | string | (none) | The tag key (must exist and apply to this kind) |
| `--value` | string | (none) | The bound value |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component setTag <name> --key key --value value
```

### `omniglass component simulation`

Commands for the simulation resource

#### `omniglass component simulation fire`

Fire an operation at a simulated component

```
omniglass component simulation fire <name> [flags]
```

Asks the simulator beside the component's node to run one operation against the simulated component, on one of its protocol surfaces: an HTTP call, a command line (SSH, Telnet, TCP) or an SNMP get, and returns its answer. The simulator answers from the component's live state in process, as its listeners would, so a command's change sticks and the collector sees it; an impairment does not stop it. Audited. Gated by simulation:update, resolved on the component tier. A component that is not simulated is a 409, a surface it does not serve a 422, and no simulator answering a 503.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--body` | string | (none) | HTTP: the request body |
| `--command` | string | (none) | SSH, Telnet or TCP: the command line |
| `--method` | string | (none) | HTTP: the method; GET when empty |
| `--oid` | string | (none) | SNMP: the OID to get |
| `--path` | string | (none) | HTTP: the request path |
| `--surface` | string | (none) | The surface to fire on, by its name in the component's surface list |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component simulation fire <name> --surface surface
```

#### `omniglass component simulation get`

Get a component's simulation

```
omniglass component simulation get <name>
```

Whether a component is simulated (it has an endpoint on a node and a product a simulator profile simulates) and, when it is, its node, address, live hits and impairment, the products its profile simulates, and its full API surface: every protocol surface, with its HTTP routes, commands and SNMP OIDs. A component that is not simulated reads simulated false. Gated by simulation:read; the component resolves within the caller's component read scope.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component simulation get <name>
```

### `omniglass component unbound-identity`

Commands for the unbound-identity resource

#### `omniglass component unbound-identity list`

List the identities a conduit reported that no binding places

```
omniglass component unbound-identity list <name>
```

A component that speaks for many owners (a conduit) lands each value its driver identifies on the owner an identity binding names; a value naming an identity it has no binding for lands on no owner and is kept here, one row per match key and value (a count, first and last heard, the keys it carried), bounded at 1024 per conduit with the least recently heard evicted, and aged out after seven days. Binding one (PUT .../identity-bindings/{key}/{value}) makes the next value naming it land on its owner. Gated by component:read; an out-of-scope conduit is a non-disclosing 404.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component unbound-identity list 'hq.$comp.meetings-cloud'
```

### `omniglass component update`

Update a component

```
omniglass component update <name> [flags]
```

Patches a component's label or product. The name is not patchable: renaming is the :rename custom method. Placement is not patchable either: relocating or re-parenting is the :move custom method, gated separately, because a placement change is an authorization act. Product is required, so it is unchanged when omitted and reclassified when named, but an explicit empty string is refused (422), not a clear. Gated by component:update; read and update scopes drive the 404 versus 403 split.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--label` | string | (none) | A new operator-facing label |
| `--product` | string | (none) | Re-classifies the component to this product (catalog SKU), by name or uuid. Required once set: an empty string is refused (422), not a clear. Explicitly-set property values persist; the new product's contract defaults follow. |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component update <name>
```

## `omniglass component-type`

Commands for the component-type resource

### `omniglass component-type create`

Create a component type

```
omniglass component-type create [flags]
```

Creates a custom (non-official) component_type, optionally under a parent. Gated by component_type:create.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--abbrev` | string | (none) | A compact form of label; omit to inherit the parent's |
| `--default-tags` | string | (none) | Tags every instance of this type starts with |
| `--icon` | string | (none) | A glyph key; omit to inherit the parent's |
| `--label` | string | (none) | What an operator reads in pickers and lists |
| `--label-rule` | string | (none) | A Go text/template rendering the label of every instance of this type, over a closed map of that component's facts (Name, Ordinal, TypeName, TypeAbbrev, Stem, ProductName, VendorName, LocationLabel, SystemTypeLabel) and the functions title, upper, lower, slug and words (words turns a kebab or snake name into the words in it, so {{title (words .Name)}} reads north-wing as North Wing). Omit to inherit the parent's, then the global component rule. A template that does not parse is refused here, 422. |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The globally unique name |
| `--parent-id` | string | (none) | The parent component_type, by name or uuid; omit for a root type |
| `--stem` | string | (none) | The auto-generated component name's prefix; omit to inherit the parent's. Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component-type create --label label --name name
```

### `omniglass component-type delete`

Delete a component type

```
omniglass component-type delete <id>
```

Deletes a custom component_type, refused if official (422, forked or not: a fork is an overlay, not ownership) or still a parent of another component_type (409). `:restore` is the only removal a shipped row admits, and it removes your fork, not the row. Gated by component_type:delete.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component-type delete display
```

### `omniglass component-type list`

List component types

```
omniglass component-type list
```

Lists the component_type registry (the taxonomy a product is classified under: mic, camera, wireless-mic under mic), ordered alphabetically by label. Each row carries its parent link, so the console reconstructs the tree client-side. Gated by component_type:read.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component-type list
```

### `omniglass component-type restore`

Restore a component type's shipped values

```
omniglass component-type restore <id>
```

Discards your fork of a shipped component_type, so reads return the values this release ships and later releases can improve them again. 409 when the row carries no fork of yours. Gated by component_type:update, the same permission that took the fork: restoring is undoing your own edit, not deleting a row.

Example:

```sh
omniglass component-type restore display
```

### `omniglass component-type update`

Update a component type

```
omniglass component-type update <id> [flags]
```

Patches a component_type's label, stem, icon, abbrev, label_rule, or default_tags. A shipped (official) row is never written: the patch FORKS it, storing your version over the shipped one, and the response comes back with forked=true under the same id. `:restore` discards the fork. Gated by component_type:update.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--abbrev` | string | (none) | A new compact form; an empty string clears it, so this type inherits the nearest ancestor's again |
| `--default-tags` | string | (none) | Replaces the default-tag set; omit to leave unchanged |
| `--icon` | string | (none) | A new glyph key; an empty string clears it, so this type inherits the nearest ancestor's again |
| `--label` | string | (none) | A new operator-facing label |
| `--label-rule` | string | (none) | A new label template; an empty string clears it, so instances fall back to the nearest ancestor's rule and then the global component rule. Refused with 422 if it does not parse. |
| `--stem` | string | (none) | A new name prefix (lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens); an empty string CLEARS it, so this type inherits the nearest ancestor's again. A root type has no ancestor to inherit from and is refused (422). |

Example:

```sh
omniglass component-type update display
```

## `omniglass driver`

Commands for the driver resource

### `omniglass driver create`

Create a driver

```
omniglass driver create [flags]
```

Creates a custom (non-official) driver. Gated by driver:create.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--label` | string | (none) | What an operator reads in pickers and lists |
| `--name` | string | (none) | The globally unique name; renameable |
| `--spec` | string | (none) | The declarative spec body; validated against the catalogs, and a spec that fails validation refuses the write (422) |
| `--version` | string | (none) | A free-form version string, e.g. 1.0.0 |

Example:

